newsitem.title: USA: NFL-CHIEFS ACQUIRE DEFENSIVE LINEMAN BUCKNER FROM STEELERS.
newsitem.headline: NFL-CHIEFS ACQUIRE DEFENSIVE LINEMAN BUCKNER FROM STEELERS.

text.p: The Kansas City Chiefs acquired defensive lineman Brentson Buckner, a starter the past two seasons at both defensive end and defensive tackle, from the Pittsburgh Steelers Friday for an undisclosed draft choice.
The 25-year-old Buckner, a second round pick out of Clemson in 1994, has amassed 101 tackles, eight sacks, three fumble recoveries and one forced fumble in his three-year NFL career.
The Chiefs were shopping for a defensive lineman with both Neil Smith and Keith Traylor testing the free agent waters.

Buckner played in 13 games and started the final five games at defensive end as a rookie in 1994. He had two sacks and was credited with six quarterback pressures, then led the team with two postseason sacks.

In 1995, Buckner started all 16 games, opening 11 at defensive end and five at nose tackle. He finished the season with three sacks and 24 quarterback pressures. Last season, he had 35 tackles, three sacks and a fumble recovery.
